stops.note: combining jagat (the world, that which moves) and natha-s (lord, master)
the name of a form of the Hindu deity Krishna/Vishnu, worshipped at a great temple in Puri, Odisha
stops.meaning: Lord of the World, the deity Jagannath

stops.note: British travelers' accounts described the deity's massive temple cart, wrongly said to crush devotees beneath its wheels
stops.meaning: the massive temple cart of Jagannath

stops.note: generalized to mean any idea, force, or institution that demands blind devotion or crushes everything in its path

current_meaning: a huge, powerful force or institution that crushes everything in its path
